artifacts.summary: Resolves all five seed design questions from live code: Mechanism A is prose-only with no enforcement; .gate-lock mutex already safely avoids contention for both narrowed --only runs and cache-hit gate 8; Move 4 structurally cannot regress onto the cache; batch admission's Mode 2 build-heavy co-scheduling excludes meta/general task types by its own task-type pre-filter. Recommends adding --skip-unchanged to Mechanism A's two emitted narrowing invocations as the sanctioned cheap probe, with no change to Move 4, no new hook, and no admission-side change.

memory_candidates.content: In orchestrate's gate pipeline, a cache-hit (--skip-unchanged) on gate 8 never acquires the specs/.gate-lock mutex: the mutex-acquire code lives inside gate8_run()'s own body, and the pre-dispatch cache-consult loop in verify-deploy.sh removes a cache-hit id from gate_registry_ids() via gate_registry_exclude_ids BEFORE the dispatch loop that would call gate8_run even runs. Likewise, tests/run-all.sh explicitly skips the gate-lock bracket entirely for any --only narrowed run. Both already structurally avoid the mutex contention that caused long implement-phase wait loops under concurrent full-sweep gate runs -- no lock-side fix is needed when adopting the cache or scoped tiers, only adoption itself.

task_is_build_heavy_implement()'s Mode 2 co-scheduling admission rule (never dispatch two build-heavy implement tasks together) is gated by a hard task_type candidacy pre-filter, BUILD_HEAVY_CANDIDATE_TASK_TYPES=("lean4" "cslib"), BEFORE its measured wall-clock signal is ever consulted. A meta/general implement task that runs a full, expensive gate sweep is never even a candidate for this refusal regardless of measured weight -- gate-heavy and build-heavy are disjoint categories in this admission rule as currently scoped.

lib/deploy-baseline-lib.sh's deploy_findings_snapshot() unconditionally strips --skip-unchanged from any caller's passthrough args (with a stderr warning), because a pre/post findings baseline comparison where one side cache-skips a gate the other ran for real would silently hide a regression on that gate. This makes the batch-gate shared capture (Move 4 / orchestrate-batch-gate.sh) structurally incapable of ever using the gate cache fast path, independent of caller discipline -- a future change proposing to speed up that capture via caching should be rejected or redirected, not implemented there.
